title: Thoughtful Traveler Choices
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Judge which of three responses best fits the six thoughtful-traveler principles in eight situations on the route, with the deciding principle named after every choice.

learningObjectives: Judge which of three responses best fits the six thoughtful-traveler principles in each of eight situations on the route, choosing the best response in at least 7 of 8 situations on the first attempt.
prerequisites: The six principles: curiosity, humility, consent, reciprocity, patience, many stories

keyQuestions: Is the tempting answer a polite way of avoiding contact?
What does this person's day look like from their side?
commonMisconceptions: Being polite means avoiding contact, such as keeping conversations brief or refusing tea.
Photographing someone from a distance is harmless because they do not notice.
Correcting a local guide with the real story is helpful.
Off-season limits are poor service rather than a normal part of the season.
A kind lie such as 'I'll come back later' is kinder than an honest no.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score on eight situations (mastery: 7 of 8).
Explain which principle the tempting Gallipoli response misses.
